permutationLabel: Tubo-ovarian abscess, sepsis, copper IUD in situ
summary: 34-year-old woman with a copper IUD, 5 days of lower abdominal pain, T 39.1, HR 118, BP 100/62, RR 22, lower peritonism, WBC 19, CRP 210, lactate 2.6; US: 6 cm complex left adnexal mass. Admit, IV antibiotics, drainage.

inputs.hpi: Five days of worsening lower abdominal pain, left more than right, fevers and rigors, offensive vaginal discharge. Copper IUD inserted 3 years ago. Serum hCG negative. Vomited twice today.

exam.general: Flushed, unwell. T 39.1, HR 118, BP 100/62, RR 22, SpO2 97%.
exam.abdomen: Lower abdominal tenderness with guarding and rebound, left worse. Bimanual: exquisite cervical motion tenderness, tender left adnexal mass.

imaging.name: USS pelvis (transvaginal)
imaging.result: 6.1 cm complex thick-walled multiloculated left adnexal mass with internal debris, consistent with tubo-ovarian abscess; moderate free fluid. IUD correctly sited.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Left tubo-ovarian abscess with sepsis (complicated PID)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Tubo-ovarian abscess (6 cm) with sepsis: admit, sepsis bundle with blood cultures, IV ceftriaxone + doxycycline + metronidazole, gynaecology; image-guided or laparoscopic drainage.

socratesAnswers.site: Lower abdomen and pelvic, left worse

mustInclude.note: TOA not responding, or large: image-guided or laparoscopic drainage.

mustExclude.note: Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan is a wrong-procedure suggestion.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Web: computeClinicalPrompts fires the 'Appendicitis — emergency surgical indication' laparoscopic-appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders, pip-tazo at induction). hasAppendicitisIndication fires on any affirmed 'guarding'/'rebound' in the abdominal exam ('guarding and rebound' from pelvic peritonitis) and ignores the confirmed diagnosis. PlanTab has no protocol for N70.03 (the PID protocol's ICD prefixes do not include it), so the documented plan is empty; only the Assessment panel (confirmed-diagnosis PID protocol) shows PID management.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Gate the appendicectomy operative-plan prompt on an appendicitis working diagnosis (as the Alvarado block does with assessmentHasAppend); guarding from torsion, PID, haemoperitoneum or DKA is not an appendicectomy indication. Add N70 to the PID protocol ICD prefixes.

mustExclude.note: An ACS, PE or AF antithrombotic/thrombolytic plan must never be attached to this diagnosis. Regression guard: this diagnosis text contains none of the substring triggers found in DiagnosisRadiationEngine ("pe", "mi", "af", …), unlike the base PID vignette ("pelvic"), so iOS is expected to pass; to be confirmed on the first iOS CI run.

guideline.name: CDC sexually transmitted infections treatment guidelines — pelvic inflammatory disease
guideline.section: Clinical diagnosis (pelvic/lower abdominal pain with cervical motion, uterine or adnexal tenderness); NAAT for N. gonorrhoeae and C. trachomatis; pregnancy test; HIV and syphilis testing; outpatient regimen ceftriaxone 500 mg IM once + doxycycline 100 mg BD 14 days + metronidazole 500 mg BD 14 days; hospitalise for tubo-ovarian abscess, severe illness or when a surgical emergency (e.g. appendicitis) cannot be excluded; parenteral regimen; partner management; IUD need not be removed
guideline.citation: Workowski KA, Bachmann LH, Chan PA, et al. Sexually transmitted infections treatment guidelines, 2021. MMWR Recomm Rep. 2021;70(4):1–187.

guideline.name: BASHH UK national guideline for the management of pelvic inflammatory disease
guideline.section: Low threshold for empirical treatment; test for gonorrhoea and chlamydia; exclude ectopic pregnancy; inpatient IV therapy for severe disease or tubo-ovarian abscess; partner notification
guideline.citation: Ross J, Cole M, Evans C, et al. United Kingdom national guideline for the management of pelvic inflammatory disease (2019 interim update). British Association for Sexual Health and HIV; 2019.

rationale: Tubo-ovarian abscess is an indication for admission and parenteral antibiotics; sepsis needs the sepsis bundle; drainage for large or non-responding abscesses.
